entries.english: Uncle / Sister / Son-in-law / Virgin / Youth (Krapf 1850, pp. 45, 47, 55, 57, 63)
entries.translation: mmétje (uncle) / úmbu (sister) / mkúe (son-in-law) / gáltama muke (virgin) / múráni (young son/warrior)

entries.english: King / Prince / Judge / Council Residence (Krapf 1850, pp. 17, 18, 23, 36, 39, 41)
entries.translation: hátju / háju / heiu (king/prince; kingdom = heiyóma; vice-regent = murra ja hatju) • manguddo (judge/ruler; judgement = yákăma) • gása ya jiháko / gassa ya heiu (residence/council seat)
bámu / muénsa (friend/comrade) • óla / jirani (neighbour) • mgéni (guest/stranger) • muntu ararsania / muelekánia (peacemaker/mediator; peace = arára / nágea)

entries.english: Breast / Shoulder / Armpit / Rib / Navel (Krapf 1850, pp. 2, 6, 30, 40, 44)
entries.translation: bágui (breast/chest) / makuáfa (shoulder; kuáfa = armpit) / yuáfu (rib) / jikófu (navel)

entries.english: Belly / Liver / Lungs / Marrow / Udder (Krapf 1850, pp. 4, 25–27, 55)
entries.translation: mahumbo (belly/stomach) / ini (liver) / ma yafu yáfu (lungs) / mora (marrow) / jiwé (udder)

entries.translation: rokánga / ukánga (sea; rukánga yukú = ocean) • kissíwa (island) • síwa ja mázi (marsh/lake) • fangáa (river bank) • gérre (coast)

entries.english: Heaven / Cloud / Wind / Lightning / Thunder (Krapf 1850, pp. 2, 7, 19, 25, 53, 61)
entries.translation: yuwíngo (heaven; wíngo, pl. mawíngo = cloud) • ruffúto / rufúto (air/wind/storm) • yuféfe (lightning) • zungurúmu (thunder) • kikúku ja pẹpo (whirlwind)

entries.english: Dawn / Morning / Noon / Evening / Morning-Star (Krapf 1850, pp. 9, 12, 29–30)
entries.translation: wiwíu (dawn/morning; wiwíde wiwiu = it dawns) • júa ya mskáhi (noon; dinner = jakúja ja mskáhi) • zioni (evening; uzuéo wa zúa = west) • nióha ya magurra (morning star)

entries.translation: mjángo (door; mjángo kadúdu = window) • tjuézi / zúezi (hedge/wall) • kinu ja ku sóa (mortar for pounding) • uzéo (sieve; fefénta na uzéo = sift) • niúngu (kettle/pot)

entries.translation: húna (cut; húna kizoa = behead; húna mnéno = decide) • iyága / iága (kill) • winsa (hunt; mawínso = hunting) • sona (sew) • andíka (write)

entries.english: Sir Harry Johnston's (1919–1922) #13 Pωkωmω (Pfωkωmω) Corpus: Prefix System, Numerals & Tana River Lexicon
entries.translation: Prefixes (Vol. I, p. 111 & Vol. II, p. 32): Class 1 Mu- (subj. mu-, u-, yu-, a-, ka-), 2 Wa-/Va-, 3 Mu-, 4 Mi-, 5 I-/Dzi-/Dz- (concord di-), 6 Ma-, 7 Ki-, 8 Vi-, 9/10 N-/Ma- (i-/zi-), 11 Lu-/U- (older Ru-/Rω-), 12 U- (for Tu-), 13 Ka-, 14 U-, 15 Ku-, 16 Ha-/Fa-/Pfa- (Hā-fa 'here', Fā-lē/Hū-kō 'there', Fēpfī 'near'), 17 Mu- • Numerals (p. 107): -mωdza (1), -wīī/-mbīī (2), -hāhū/N-tāhū (3), -nē/N-nē (4), -tsānω (5), Hāndāhū (6), Fūṅgāhē (7), Nānē (8), K-ēnda (9), Kūmi (10), Mī-rōṅgω mī-wīī (20), Gāna (100), Kī-kwī (1,000) • Distinctive Roots (pp. 98–110): Sempfe (adze), Dzahe/Tsahi (arrow), Tsωka/Berya (axe), M-fūwe pl. va-fūwe (baboon), Hōri/Zefe (canoe), Hacu/Haju (chief), M-pfūya (rain), Tsāna/Dzāna (river), Phēra (rhinoceros), Rē pl. ma-rē (sheep), Wānte/N-gāω (shield), Mū-hūma (slave), U-tēmbo (palm wine), Kī-vīnω (song), Lū-khūni/Lū-kūni (firewood, Errata p. x), Yēω (today), Kēšω (tomorrow), Dzāna (yesterday), Nhā-nhā! (no!)
entries.pronunciation: ki-pfω-kω-mω / ha-cu / m-pfu-ya / tsa-na / ha-nda-hu / fu-nga-he
entries.context: Sir Harry H. Johnston, 'A Comparative Study of the Bantu and Semi-Bantu Languages' (Vol. I, 1919, pp. 98–112; Vol. II, 1922, pp. 31–32)

entries.english: Dr. J. L. Krapf's (1850, Preface pp. iv, vii–viii & pp. 1–64) Kipokómo Corpus from Hadji Omar of Kalindi & Mángea Origin Traditions
entries.translation: Historical Context (Preface pp. vii–viii): Recorded in 1845 at Takaóngo (near Kilifi Bay) from Hadji Omar, brother of Bonnaia Dadia, chief of Kalindi (first Pokomo village on the Dana / Pokómo / Máro / Quilimancy river), who served as interpreter with the Galla chieftain of Berraráta; preserves the oral traditions that the Wasegéju near Tanga were originally Wapokómo expelled by the Galla, that the Wateita of Kadiáro, Ndara, and Bura call the Wanika Ambakómo from their former residence in Pokomo territory, and that the Kiriama (Giriama) lived at Mángea on the Pokomóni • Distinctive Kipokómo Governance, Kinship & Cushitic-Sabaki Lexicon (pp. 1–64): hátju / heiu (king/chief; heiyóma = kingdom; murra ja hatju = vice-regent; gása ya jiháko / gassa ya heiu = chief's council seat), manguddo (judge; yákăma = judgement, yakámisa = judge), kallu (soothsaying, p. 47), arára & nágea (peace/reconciliation; muntu ararsania = peacemaker, p. 33), zahuáje (grandfather), tjáuje (grandmother/mistress), mmétje (uncle), úmbu (sister), gáltama muke (virgin), múráni (young son/warrior), bámu (friend), óla (neighbour), mágu (news/information), sári (name), mótjo (heart/mind/soul), muázi (blood), gégo pl. magégo (tooth), zuátjo pl. niátjo (footprint/sole), zána (river), rokánga / ukánga (sea/ocean), dau & mzéfe (ship/mtepe), kibéria (axe), kéra (iron), harre (donkey), férada (horse), sánga (bull), korma (ox), nadóde (leopard), maiónda (monkey), kitungúe (hare), ungúu jua zána (hippo), uissoa (flour), kilizuío (breakfast), jakúja ja mskáhi (dinner), jakúja ja zióni (supper), huáa & hikísa (accept/take), zákka (love/want), látja (search/seek), hasáua (converse)
entries.pronunciation: ka-lin-di • bon-na-ia da-dia • ha-dji o-mar • man-ge-a • am-ba-ko-mo • ha-tju • man-gud-do
entries.context: Rev. Dr. J. L. Krapf (1850) "Vocabulary of Six East-African Languages (Kisuáheli, Kiníka, Kikámba, Kipokómo, Kihiáu, Kigálla)" (Tübingen, L. F. Fues), Preface pp. iv, vii–viii & pp. 1–64
